current_sections.Statement:
Fix $t\ge1$. Suppose the selected empirical array at time $t-1$ has the CLT with covariance $\widehat V_{t-1}$ for $k_t\psi$. Let $\psi:\Theta_t\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $\widetilde\pi_t(|\psi|^{2+\delta})<\infty$ for some $\delta>0$ and $k_t\psi\in\Phi_{t-1}^{(1)}$. Then the proposal empirical mean after mutation satisfies
$$\sqrt N\left(\eta_t^N(\psi)-\widetilde\pi_t(\psi)\right)\Rightarrow N\!\left(0,\widehat V_{t-1}(k_t\psi)+\pi_{t-1}\!\left(\operatorname{Var}_{k_t}(\psi)\right)\right)=N(0,\widetilde V_t(\psi)).$$
In particular, if $\phi\in\Psi_t^{(1)}$ and $1\in\Phi_s^{(1)}$ for $0\le s\le t$, the weighted corrected estimate satisfies
$$\sqrt N\left(\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\right)\Rightarrow N(0,V_t(\phi)).$$
At $t=0$, for $\phi\in\Psi_0^{(1)}$ the weighted estimate has the ratio CLT with covariance $V_0(\phi)=\widetilde V_0(\upsilon_0(\phi-\pi_0\phi))$.
current_sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The finite-horizon particle scheme, the previous selected-population CLT, and the function-class hypotheses in the Statement.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is inherited through the finite-horizon particle-law construction and the Lindeberg–Feller supplier.

[F1] [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]: $\widetilde\pi_t=\pi_{t-1}k_t$, $\pi_t=\upsilon_t\widetilde\pi_t$, and $\Psi_t$ supplies a target $2+\epsilon$ moment and recursive membership of $k_t(\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi))$ in $\Psi_{t-1}$.

[F2] [[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]]: Conditional on the selected parents, the next proposal particles are drawn independently through $k_t$ and are then corrected by the incremental RN weights.

[F3] [[lem-smc-finite-horizon-empirical-law]]: Integrable proposal and selected empirical averages converge in probability to their target-law integrals at each fixed time.

[F4] [[thm-lindeberg-feller-central-limit-theorem-sufficiency]]: A centered independent triangular array with positive total variance and the Lindeberg condition, divided by its row standard deviation, converges to $N(0,1)$.

[F5] [[thm-slutsky-for-real-random-variables]]: If $X_N\Rightarrow X$ and $Y_N\to c$ in probability, then $X_NY_N\Rightarrow cX$; for $c\ne0$, the corresponding ratio converges to $X/c$.

[F6] [[cor-chebyshev-inequality-for-random-variables]]: For a square-integrable variable on any probability space, the probability of an absolute centered deviation at least $a>0$ is at most its variance divided by $a^2$.
current_sections.Proof:
**Given:** The hypotheses in the Statement.

1.1 At $t=0$, the centered weighted numerator $Z=\upsilon_0(\phi-\pi_0\phi)$ has mean zero and a finite $2+\epsilon$ moment by the definition of $\Psi_0$. If its variance is positive, [F4] gives the IID CLT; if its variance is zero, [F6] gives convergence of its centered sample mean to zero. The denominator $\eta_0^N(\upsilon_0)$ converges to one by [F3], since $\widetilde\pi_0(\upsilon_0)=1$. Slutsky [F5] gives the ratio CLT with variance $V_0(\phi)$. For $t\ge1$, $\Phi_t$ is closed under finite linear combinations: use the smaller moment exponent, the $L^p$ triangle inequality, and linearity of kernel integration. The same arguments together with the target-moment condition show closure of $\Psi_t$. If $\phi\in\Psi_t$, then $\psi=\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi)$ has a finite proposal $2+\delta$ moment because $\phi,1\in\Phi_t$, and $k_t\psi=E_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi)\in\Psi_{t-1}$ by the recursive $\Psi_t$ condition. [A1, F1, F3, F4, F5, F6, given, algebra]

2.1 For the mutation part, condition on the selected parent paths $\check X_{t-1}^{1:N}$ and set $m_i=k_t\psi(\check X_{t-1}^i)$. Under the product kernel in [F2], $D_{i,N}=\psi(X_t^i)-m_i$ are independent and centered. Their row variance is
$$s_N^2=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\operatorname{Var}_{k_t(\check X_{t-1}^i)}(\psi),$$
which converges in probability to $\sigma^2=\pi_{t-1}(\operatorname{Var}_{k_t}(\psi))$ by [F3], because $0\le\operatorname{Var}_{k_t}(\psi)\le k_t(\psi^2)$ and $\pi_{t-1}(k_t|\psi|^{2+\delta})=\widetilde\pi_t(|\psi|^{2+\delta})<\infty$. When $\sigma^2>0$, normalize the array by $s_N\sqrt N$, where $s_N^2$ is the displayed variance. For every $a>0$, the resulting conditional Lindeberg sum is at most
$$C_\delta a^{-\delta}N^{-\delta/2}s_N^{-(2+\delta)}\,\check\eta_{t-1}^N(k_t|\psi|^{2+\delta}),$$
where $C_\delta$ is a finite constant from $|a-b|^{2+\delta}\le2^{1+\delta}(|a|^{2+\delta}+|b|^{2+\delta})$ and Jensen's inequality. Since $s_N\to\sigma>0$ and [F3] makes the average factor converge in probability to a finite value, this conditional Lindeberg sum tends to zero. [A1, F1, F2, F3, given]

2.2 Along any subsequence, choose a further subsequence on which $s_N\to\sigma$ almost surely. If $\sigma>0$, a further subsequence makes the normalized Lindeberg sums converge almost surely; [F4] gives a standard-normal limit for the normalized row, and Slutsky [F5] with $s_N\to\sigma$ gives the conditional characteristic-function limit $e^{-u^2\sigma^2/2}$. If $\sigma=0$, conditional [F6] gives
$$P\!\left(\left|N^{-1/2}\sum_iD_{i,N}\right|>a\,\middle|\,\check X_{t-1}^{1:N}\right)\le\min(1,s_N^2/a^2)\longrightarrow0$$
for every $a>0$, yielding the same characteristic-function limit with variance zero. The subsequence criterion therefore gives convergence in probability of the conditional characteristic functions along the full sequence. They are bounded by one, so their $L^1$ differences from that limit also tend to zero. [F4, F5, F6, step 2.1, algebra]

2.3 The conditional mean part is
$$P_N=\sqrt N\left(\check\eta_{t-1}^N(k_t\psi)-\pi_{t-1}(k_t\psi)\right),$$
and has the previous selected-population CLT by the hypothesis of the Statement. The total proposal error is $P_N+N^{-1/2}\sum_iD_{i,N}$. Multiplying the conditional characteristic function from step 2.2 by the bounded factor $e^{iuP_N}$ and integrating shows that its limit is the product of the previous Gaussian characteristic function and $e^{-u^2\sigma^2/2}$. Hence the two covariance contributions add, giving $\widetilde V_t(\psi)$. [F1, F2, step 2.2, given]

3.1 For $\phi\in\Psi_t$, apply the mutation result to $\psi=\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi)$ using step 1.1 and the preceding selected CLT for $k_t\psi\in\Psi_{t-1}$. By [F3], $\eta_t^N(\upsilon_t)\to\widetilde\pi_t(\upsilon_t)=1$ in probability, and the event of a zero denominator has probability tending to zero. On its complement,
$$\sqrt N\left(\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\right)=\frac{\sqrt N\,\eta_t^N(\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi))}{\eta_t^N(\upsilon_t)}.$$
Slutsky [F5] gives the stated limit with covariance $\widetilde V_t(\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi))=V_t(\phi)$. The fallback on a zero empirical weight sum changes the ratio only on an event whose probability tends to zero. [F1, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 2.3, algebra] ∎

current_sections.Statement:
Fix a time $t$ in the finite-horizon SIR system of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]. Let $\omega_t^N$ be its corrected weighted empirical law and let $\check\eta_t^N$ be the empirical law after multinomial offspring resampling. Suppose $\phi\in\Psi_t^{(1)}$, the empirical-law conclusions of [[lem-smc-finite-horizon-empirical-law]] hold, and
$$\sqrt N\{\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,V)$$
for a finite $V\ge0$. Then
$$\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\omega_t^N(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\phi)),$$
asymptotically independently of the weighted-estimator fluctuation, and
$$\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N\!\left(0,V+\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\phi)\right).$$
current_sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The corrected weighted empirical law, the multinomial selection rule, the target-moment condition $\phi\in\Psi_t^{(1)}$, and the weighted-estimator CLT in the Statement.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is inherited through the finite-horizon particle-law construction and the cited probability limit theorem.

[F1] [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]: $\Psi_t^{(1)}$ gives $\pi_t(|\phi|^{2+\epsilon})<\infty$ for some $\epsilon>0$.

[F2] [[alg-multinomial-and-residual-offspring-resampling]]: Conditional on the corrected particles, multinomial offspring are IID draws from $\omega_t^N$.

[F3] [[lem-smc-finite-horizon-empirical-law]]: For every $\pi_t$-integrable test $h$, $\omega_t^N(h)\to\pi_t(h)$ in probability.

[F4] [[thm-lindeberg-feller-central-limit-theorem-sufficiency]]: A centered independent triangular array with positive total variance and the Lindeberg condition, divided by its row standard deviation, converges to $N(0,1)$.

[F5] [[cor-chebyshev-inequality-for-random-variables]]: For a square-integrable variable on any probability space, the probability of an absolute centered deviation at least $a>0$ is at most its variance divided by $a^2$.

[F6] [[thm-slutsky-for-real-random-variables]]: Multiplying a distributionally convergent real variable by one converging in probability to a constant gives the scaled limit.
current_sections.Proof:
**Given:** The hypotheses in the Statement.

1.1 Let $\mathcal F_N$ contain the corrected particles and their weights. By [F2], conditionally on $\mathcal F_N$ the selected values $Y_1^N,\ldots,Y_N^N$ are IID with law $\omega_t^N$. Their centered conditional variance is $s_N^2=\omega_t^N(\phi^2)-\omega_t^N(\phi)^2$, which converges in probability to $s^2=\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\phi)$ by [F1] and [F3]. [A1, F1, F2, F3, given]

1.2 Put $\xi_i^N=\phi(Y_i^N)-\omega_t^N(\phi)$. Since $\pi_t(|\phi|^{2+\epsilon})<\infty$, [F3] gives $\omega_t^N(|\phi|^{2+\epsilon})=O_P(1)$ and $\omega_t^N(|\phi|)=O_P(1)$. Jensen's inequality and $|a-b|^{2+\epsilon}\le 2^{1+\epsilon}(|a|^{2+\epsilon}+|b|^{2+\epsilon})$ then give $\omega_t^N(|\phi-\omega_t^N(\phi)|^{2+\epsilon})=O_P(1)$. For every $a>0$, the conditional Lindeberg sum is bounded by
$$\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbb E\!\left[(\xi_i^N)^2\mathbf1_{\{|\xi_i^N|>a\sqrt N\}}\middle|\mathcal F_N\right]\le a^{-\epsilon}N^{-\epsilon/2}\omega_t^N(|\phi-\omega_t^N(\phi)|^{2+\epsilon}),$$
which tends to zero in probability. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 Along any subsequence, choose a further subsequence on which $s_N\to s$ almost surely. If $s>0$, then eventually $s_N>s/2$; the normalized Lindeberg sum for draws divided by $s_N\sqrt N$ is bounded by step 1.2 at threshold $as/2$, divided by $s_N^2$. It therefore tends to zero in probability, and a further subsequence makes that convergence almost sure. Apply [F4] to obtain a standard-normal limit for the normalized row. Slutsky [F6] with $s_N\to s$ gives convergence of the conditional characteristic function of $N^{-1/2}\sum_i\xi_i^N$ to $e^{-u^2s^2/2}$. If $s=0$, conditional [F5] gives $P(|N^{-1/2}\sum_i\xi_i^N|>a\mid\mathcal F_N)\le\min(1,s_N^2/a^2)\to0$, giving the degenerate characteristic-function limit. The subsequence criterion therefore gives convergence in probability of these conditional characteristic functions along the full sequence. [F4, F5, F6, step 1.1, step 1.2]

2.2 The conditional characteristic functions are bounded by one, so their differences from $e^{-u^2s^2/2}$ converge to zero in $L^1$. Multiplying by the bounded factor $e^{iu\sqrt N(\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi))}$ and taking expectations shows that the joint limiting characteristic function factors into the weighted-estimator Gaussian characteristic function and $e^{-u^2s^2/2}$. Thus the resampling fluctuation is asymptotically independent of the weighted fluctuation, and their sum has variance $V+s^2$. [step 2.1, given, algebra] ∎

current_sections.Statement:
Fix a time $t$ in the finite-horizon SIR system of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]. Let $X_t^{1:N}$ have proposal empirical law $\eta_t^N$, corrected law $\omega_t^N$, and residual-resampled law $\check\eta_t^N$. Assume the proposal empirical law converges in probability for every integrable test as in [[lem-smc-finite-horizon-empirical-law]], the weighted estimate has a finite-variance CLT
$$\sqrt N\{\omega_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,V),$$
and $\phi\in\Psi_t^{(1)}$. Write $u=\upsilon_t$ and assume either $u=1$ $\widetilde\pi_t$-almost everywhere, or
$$\widetilde\pi_t(u\in\{1,2,\ldots\})=0.$$
In the second case $c=\widetilde\pi_t(r(u))>0$. Then, with
$$R_t(\phi)=\widetilde\pi_t(r(u)\phi^2)-\frac{\widetilde\pi_t(r(u)\phi)^2}{c},$$
where $R_t(\phi)=0$ in the constant-weight case,
$$\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\omega_t^N(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,R_t(\phi)),$$
asymptotically independently of the weighted-estimator fluctuation, and
$$\sqrt N\{\check\eta_t^N(\phi)-\pi_t(\phi)\}\Rightarrow N(0,V+R_t(\phi)).$$
current_sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The proposal empirical-law convergence, the weighted-estimator CLT, the recursive target-moment condition, and the residual offspring algorithm in the Statement.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is inherited through the finite-horizon particle-law construction and the cited probability limit theorem.

[F1] [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]: $u=d\pi_t/d\widetilde\pi_t$, $\widetilde\pi_t(u)=1$, $r(v)=v-\lfloor v\rfloor$, and the formal residual candidate is assigned as $R_t$ only in the no-positive-integer-atom branch or the constant-weight branch.

[F2] [[alg-multinomial-and-residual-offspring-resampling]]: For normalized weights $\rho_i$, residual resampling gives each particle $\lfloor N\rho_i\rfloor$ deterministic copies and fills the remaining count with IID draws proportional to $r(N\rho_i)$.

[F3] [[lem-smc-finite-horizon-empirical-law]]: The proposal and corrected empirical laws converge in probability for integrable tests.

[F4] [[thm-lindeberg-feller-central-limit-theorem-sufficiency]]: A centered independent triangular array with positive total variance and the Lindeberg condition, divided by its row standard deviation, converges to $N(0,1)$.

[F5] [[cor-chebyshev-inequality-for-random-variables]]: For a square-integrable variable on any probability space, the probability of an absolute centered deviation at least $a>0$ is at most its variance divided by $a^2$.

[F6] [[thm-slutsky-for-real-random-variables]]: Multiplying a distributionally convergent real variable by one converging in probability to a constant gives the scaled limit.
current_sections.Proof:
**Given:** The hypotheses in the Statement.

1.1 Put $\bar u_N=\eta_t^N(u)$ and $b_i^N=r(u(X_t^i)/\bar u_N)$ on the event $\bar u_N>0$, whose probability tends to one by [F3]. If $u=1$ almost everywhere, every finite normalized weight is $1/N$ and residual selection is deterministic, so the resampling fluctuation is zero. In the other case, for $j=0,1,2,2+\epsilon$, where $\pi_t(|\phi|^{2+\epsilon})<\infty$, one has
$$\frac1N\sum_i b_i^N\phi(X_t^i)^j\xrightarrow{P}\widetilde\pi_t(r(u)\phi^j).$$
To verify this triangular empirical limit, fix $M$ and first restrict to $u\le M$ and $|\phi|\le M$. The compact $u$ interval meets only finitely many positive-integer discontinuities of $r$. Delete open $\gamma$-neighborhoods of those integers. On the remaining compact set, $r(u/\bar u_N)\to r(u)$ uniformly as $\bar u_N\to1$, and $|\phi|^j\le M^j$, so [F3] gives convergence of the restricted averages. Each deleted neighborhood has proposal integral of $|\phi|^j$ tending to zero as $\gamma\downarrow0$: it lies where $u\ge1/2$, and $\widetilde\pi_t(u|\phi|^j)=\pi_t(|\phi|^j)<\infty$; the no-atom condition gives the limit zero. [F3] controls its empirical average for each fixed $\gamma$. For the tails, when $\bar u_N\in[1/2,2]$, $b_i^N\le2u(X_t^i)$; hence the $|\phi|>M$ contribution is bounded by $2\eta_t^N(u|\phi|^j\mathbf1_{\{|\phi|>M\}})$, whose limit tends to zero by target integrability. On $u>M$, use $b_i^N\le1$ and $\widetilde\pi_t(|\phi|^j\mathbf1_{\{u>M\}})\le M^{-1}\pi_t(|\phi|^j)$, with [F3] again controlling the empirical average. The corresponding target tails obey the same bounds because $r(u)\le u$ and $r(u)\le1$. Taking first $N\to\infty$, then $\gamma\downarrow0$ and $M\to\infty$, proves the claim. [F1, F3, given, algebra]

1.2 Taking $j=0$ in step 1.1 gives $N^{-1}\sum_i b_i^N\to c$. Here $c>0$: if $c=0$, then $u$ is integer-valued almost surely; the no-positive-integer-atom assumption would force $u=0$ almost surely, contradicting $\widetilde\pi_t(u)=1$. Thus the number $M_N=\sum_i b_i^N$ of residual draws diverges and $M_N/N\to c$. Their conditional sampling probabilities are $b_i^N/M_N$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 Let $m_N=M_N^{-1}\sum_i b_i^N\phi(X_t^i)$. Given the particles, the residual offspring contribution to the centered, $\sqrt N$-scaled empirical mean is $N^{-1/2}\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_N}(\phi(Y_\ell^N)-m_N)$, with IID conditional draws $Y_\ell^N$ from probabilities $b_i^N/M_N$. By step 1.1 its conditional variance converges in probability to
$$c\left\{\frac{\widetilde\pi_t(r(u)\phi^2)}c-\left(\frac{\widetilde\pi_t(r(u)\phi)}c\right)^2\right\}=R_t(\phi).$$
The empirical $(2+\epsilon)$-moment $N^{-1}\sum_i b_i^N|\phi(X_t^i)|^{2+\epsilon}$ is bounded in probability by step 1.1, and $M_N/N\to c>0$. The residual draw mean $m_N$ is bounded in probability by the $j=1$ limit. Therefore the conditional $(2+\epsilon)$ moment of $\phi(Y_\ell^N)-m_N$ is bounded in probability. For any $a>0$, the Lindeberg sum is at most $a^{-\epsilon}N^{-\epsilon/2}(M_N/N)\mathbb E[|\phi(Y_1^N)-m_N|^{2+\epsilon}\mid X_t^{1:N}]$, so it tends to zero. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 Along any subsequence, choose a further subsequence on which the conditional residual variance converges almost surely. If $R_t(\phi)>0$, the conditional standard deviation is eventually greater than $\sqrt{R_t(\phi)}/2$. Apply the bound in step 2.1 at threshold $a\sqrt{R_t(\phi)}/2$ and divide by the conditional variance; this gives the Lindeberg condition after normalizing the residual sum by its conditional standard deviation. Conditional [F4] gives a standard-normal limit, and Slutsky [F6] with the conditional standard deviation converging to $\sqrt{R_t(\phi)}$ gives the characteristic-function limit $e^{-u_0^2R_t(\phi)/2}$. If $R_t(\phi)=0$, conditional [F5] bounds the deviation probability by the conditional variance divided by the squared threshold, giving the same degenerate limit. AC is inherited only through the particle law and conditional CLT supplier [F4]; the finite residual calculation adds no choice. The subsequence criterion gives convergence in probability along the full sequence. These conditional characteristic functions are bounded by one. Multiplication by the characteristic factor of the weighted-estimator fluctuation and integration therefore shows asymptotic independence and adds $R_t(\phi)$ to $V$. The deterministic-floor part is centered at its conditional expectation, so the conditional mean of the selected empirical law is exactly $\omega_t^N(\phi)$. [A1, F2, F4, F5, F6, given, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

current_sections.Statement:
Use the operators and multinomial variance recursion of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]] at every selection time. For $\phi\in\Psi_t^{(d)}$, put $\bar\phi=\phi-\pi_t(\phi)$. Then
$$V_t(\phi)=\sum_{k=0}^{t}\widetilde\pi_k\!\left[\upsilon_k^2\,E_{k+1:t}(\bar\phi)E_{k+1:t}(\bar\phi)^\top\right],$$
where the $k=t$ term uses $E_{t+1:t}\bar\phi=\bar\phi$. Each summand is a finite positive-semidefinite matrix under the stated class conditions.
current_sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The finite-horizon target/proposal flow, Radon–Nikodym weights, forward operators, and multinomial covariance recursion in the cited definition.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is inherited through the finite-horizon path and Radon–Nikodym construction.

[F1] [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]: $\upsilon_s=d\pi_s/d\widetilde\pi_s$, $E_s h=k_s(\upsilon_sh)$, $\pi_{s-1}E_sh=\pi_s h$, and $\widehat V_{s-1}^{\mathrm{multi}}=V_{s-1}+\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_{s-1}}$; $\Psi_t$ recursively supplies the target moments of the centered backward images.
current_sections.Proof:
**Given:** The hypotheses in the Statement.

1.1 For every integrable $h$ on $\Theta_s$, the Radon–Nikodym identity [F1] gives $\pi_{s-1}(E_sh)=\pi_{s-1}(k_s(\upsilon_sh))=\widetilde\pi_s(\upsilon_sh)=\pi_s(h)$. Hence if $\pi_s(h)=0$, then $E_sh$ has mean zero under $\pi_{s-1}$. [A1, F1, given]

1.2 For a square-integrable vector function $u$ on $\Theta_s$, expand
$$u-\widetilde\pi_s(u)=\bigl(u-k_su\bigr)+\bigl(k_su-\widetilde\pi_s(u)\bigr).$$
The cross-covariance terms vanish after integrating the first factor conditionally against $k_s$, because $k_s(u-k_su)=0$. Therefore
$$\operatorname{Cov}_{\widetilde\pi_s}(u)=\int\operatorname{Cov}_{k_s}(u)(x)\,\pi_{s-1}(dx)+\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_{s-1}}(k_su).$$
For $u=\upsilon_s h$ with $\pi_s(h)=0$, its $\widetilde\pi_s$ mean is zero by step 1.1. Substituting the multinomial recursion from [F1] thus yields
$$V_s(h)=V_{s-1}(E_sh)+\widetilde\pi_s\!\left[\upsilon_s^2hh^\top\right].$$
[F1, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 Starting with $h=\bar\phi$ at time $t$, apply step 1.1 to see that each backward iterate $E_{k+1:t}\bar\phi$ has $\pi_k$-mean zero. The recursive $\Psi$ condition also gives its finite target second moment at each such time. Repeated substitution of the one-step identity in step 1.2 gives one new term $\widetilde\pi_k[\upsilon_k^2(E_{k+1:t}\bar\phi)(E_{k+1:t}\bar\phi)^\top]$ at each $k=t,t-1,\ldots,1$, and the remaining initial term is $V_0(E_{1:t}\bar\phi)=\operatorname{Cov}_{\widetilde\pi_0}(\upsilon_0E_{1:t}\bar\phi)$. Its mean is zero by step 1.1, so it equals the $k=0$ summand. The same base calculation gives the formula when $t=0$. Each summand is finite: for $k\ge1$, the recursive $\Phi$ condition gives a $2+\delta$ proposal moment of $\upsilon_kE_{k+1:t}\bar\phi$; for $k=0$, the initial $\Psi_0$ moment gives square integrability of $\upsilon_0E_{1:t}\bar\phi$. [A1, F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, induction, algebra] ∎

held_items.reason: Escalated to owner: this carrier proves a separate bound under uniform incremental-weight and backward-operator contraction hypotheses. It does not establish the plan's Theorem 5 claim from predecessor density ratios and likelihood bounds; cex-smc-time-bound-fails-with-varying-proposals refutes those displayed conditions.

current_sections.Statement:
Use multinomial offspring resampling at every time and the variance $V_t$ in [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]. Assume there is a constant $B<\infty$ such that $\upsilon_s\le B$ $\widetilde\pi_s$-almost everywhere for every $s\ge0$. Assume also that the forward operators satisfy the uniform oscillation condition of [[lem-smc-backward-operator-oscillation-bound]] with one $\beta\in[0,1)$ for all times. Then every bounded real test $\phi$ with $\Delta\phi=\sup\phi-\inf\phi<\infty$ satisfies
$$V_t(\phi)\le\frac{B^2(\Delta\phi)^2}{1-\beta^2}\qquad(t\ge0).$$
This is a bound on the fixed-horizon CLT variance, uniform in the time index; it is not a finite-particle error bound.
current_sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The multinomial SMC flow, the uniform incremental-weight bound $B$, and the uniform forward-operator oscillation coefficient $\beta<1$.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: AC is inherited through the finite-horizon SMC path-law and Radon–Nikodym construction.

[F1] [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]: $V_t$ is the weighted-estimator covariance, $\upsilon_s$ is the normalized incremental Radon–Nikodym weight, and $\Phi_s,\Psi_s$ are the recursive moment classes.

[F2] [[lem-smc-multinomial-variance-unrolls]]: $V_t(\phi)$ is the sum over $k=0,\ldots,t$ of $\widetilde\pi_k[\upsilon_k^2(E_{k+1:t}(\phi-\pi_t\phi))^2]$.

[F3] [[lem-smc-backward-operator-oscillation-bound]]: $\|E_{k+1:t}(\phi-\pi_t\phi)\|_\infty\le\beta^{t-k}\Delta\phi$.
current_sections.Proof:
**Given:** The hypotheses in the Statement.

1.1 Uniformly bounded weights and bounded $\phi$ imply $\phi\in\Psi_s$ at each finite time: every weighted proposal moment is finite, the initial weighted moment is finite because $\upsilon_0\le B$, the target moments are finite, and every forward image of a bounded test is bounded by $B$ times its sup norm. The constant test also belongs to each $\Psi_s$. Thus the unrolling formula [F2] applies. By [F2],
$$V_t(\phi)=\sum_{k=0}^t\widetilde\pi_k\!\left[\upsilon_k^2\left(E_{k+1:t}(\phi-\pi_t\phi)\right)^2\right].$$
The summands are nonnegative and finite because $\upsilon_k\le B$ almost everywhere and $\phi$ is bounded. [A1, F1, F2, given]

2.1 For each $k$, [F3] bounds its summand by $B^2\beta^{2(t-k)}(\Delta\phi)^2$. Therefore
$$V_t(\phi)\le B^2(\Delta\phi)^2\sum_{j=0}^t\beta^{2j}\le\frac{B^2(\Delta\phi)^2}{1-\beta^2},$$
which is independent of $t$. [F1, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎
current_sections.Remarks: The extra uniform bound on incremental weights and the explicit backward-operator contraction are stated hypotheses. The density-ratio and likelihood bounds in the BCS-42 design do not, by themselves, imply a uniform incremental-weight bound when the proposal kernels vary with time; the assigned B page gives a finite-state counterexample. That source-scope discrepancy is recorded for owner reconciliation.

original_design_section:
### BCS-42 — Finite-horizon SMC error, CLTs, and degeneracy
**Pages:** smc-clts-error-and-degeneracy / smc-clts-error-and-degeneracy-examples. **Scope:** State Chopin's fixed-horizon $H\to\infty$ particle-count CLT with targets $\pi_t$, proposal laws $\tilde\pi_t$, incremental weights $\upsilon_t=d\pi_t/d\tilde\pi_t$, and mutation kernels $k_t$. For vector-valued $\phi$, initialize $\Phi_0^{(d)}=\{\phi:E_{\tilde\pi_0}\|\phi\|^2<\infty\}$ and recursively require $\phi\in\Phi_t^{(d)}$ if for some $\delta>0$, $E_{\tilde\pi_t}\|\upsilon_t\phi\|^{2+\delta}<\infty$ and $\theta_{t-1}\mapsto E_{k_t(\theta_{t-1},\cdot)}[\upsilon_t\phi]$ belongs to $\Phi_{t-1}^{(d)}$. Require $1\in\Phi_t^{(1)}$ at every time. Give the exact variance recursion $\widetilde V_0(\phi)=\operatorname{Var}_{\tilde\pi_0}(\phi)$, $\widetilde V_t(\phi)=\widehat V_{t-1}(E_{k_t}\phi)+E_{\pi_{t-1}}[\operatorname{Var}_{k_t}(\phi)]$, $V_t(\phi)=\widetilde V_t(\upsilon_t(\phi-\pi_t\phi))$, and, for multinomial resampling, $\widehat V_t(\phi)=V_t(\phi)+\operatorname{Var}_{\pi_t}(\phi)$. For residual resampling replace the last term by $R_t(\phi)=E_{\tilde\pi_t}[r(\upsilon_t)\phi\phi^T]-E_{\tilde\pi_t}[r(\upsilon_t)\phi]E_{\tilde\pi_t}[r(\upsilon_t)\phi]^T/E_{\tilde\pi_t}[r(\upsilon_t)]$, where $r(u)=u-\lfloor u\rfloor$, so $\widehat V_t=V_t+R_t$ when $E_{\tilde\pi_t}r(\upsilon_t)>0$; if this expectation is zero, all residual offspring counts are deterministic and define $R_t=0$. State both source CLT outputs (weighted estimate variance $V_t$ and post-resampling unweighted estimate variance $\widehat V_t$), centered at $\pi_t\phi$. For a separate bounded-asymptotic-variance-in-time result, require finite test oscillation $\Delta\phi$, uniform transition and proposal density ratios $g(x|x')/g(x|x'')\le C$, $q_t(x|x')/q_t(x|x'')\le C$, and likelihoods $0<f\le f(y|x)\le\bar f$; this is Chopin Theorem 5's restrictive asymptotic-variance condition, not a general finite-$N$ time-uniform error bound. ESS is weight concentration, not posterior coverage/variance/convergence; a fixed-horizon CLT is not a uniform-in-time accuracy guarantee. **Proof route:** Conditional triangular-array CLT/Lindeberg at each step, recursive moment closure and variance recursion; long-time asymptotic-variance bound additionally uses the source's Feynman–Kac contraction conditions. **Examples:** dominant weight, ancestry collapse, fixed-time versus long-horizon degradation, bounded-weight case. **Requires:** BCS-41; `thm-lindeberg-feller-central-limit-theorem-sufficiency`, `thm-martingale-central-limit-theorem`, `thm-conditional-expectation-exists-by-radon-nikodym`, `def-conditional-expectation-as-an-ae-class`, `thm-tower-property-of-conditional-expectation`. **Sources:** Chopin (2004), Theorems 1–2, 4–5 and Appendices A.1/A.3–A.4, source PDF pp. 7–14, 27–31; Doucet–Johansen §3 CLT displays refer elsewhere for proof.
